scope: Seven frozen production-file typed frame metadata increment. No production editing, IDF build, hardware, commit or claimed BLE throughput result. Existing Wi-Fi owner dependency P1 remains separately open.

findings.evidence: AsyncLog builds a packet only after successful sensorarrayTextProtocolBuildFrame for the frame stored in the source slot; PopFrame returns the same copied frame/packet. NetFramePublish validates packet length/tag/comma and sequence versus the frame, then creates stack POD metadata. Only bounded synchronous deep copying occurs before return. The helper does not query global live configuration.

FramePublicationMetadata explicitly copies C/M legacy generation/requestId from configSnapshot, V/R from measurement.modeGeneration/modeRequestId, and M profile pair from rowProfileGeneration/rowProfileRequestId. ApplyFrameMetadata preserves M rgen/pgen already present before extension; the immutable identity is retained independently for protection. Deliberately disagreeing domains in 96 real-encoder synthetic cases exactly match old parser output.

ApplyFrameMetadata uses identity.revision!=0 exactly as TextAppendIdentity; omitted C/V/R extension fields become zero, while M rows/profile fields remain. Revision zero/distinct/max, all 1-8 rows and C/V/R/M passed; session remains a validated nonzero typed identity, as required by the previous identity-only API.

Encoder source hash is unchanged. The typed helper validates only constant-size metadata/input boundaries, not arbitrary wire syntax/CRC. This is documented and limited to successful real encoder packet/frame pairs. The previous ParseFrameMeta was also not a wire/CRC authorization gate: failure cleared hasFrameMeta without rejecting general publication. Legacy PublishData and identity-only PublishFrame still call it.

Metadata applies to an allocated private Transport slot before descriptor enqueue. Identity is copied into slot storage; no stack POD pointer escapes. Failed second-stage metadata validation releases that descriptor. Tests mutate producer frame/packet after publication and confirm queued bytes and every metadata field unchanged; unchanged source/transport held/WRITING/queue pressure/expiry tests also passed. Pool counts/layout and BLE ownership code are unchanged.

Both legacy-parsed and typed slots produce identical SHORT output or identical unsupported result for each of 96 real frames. Normal previews and full protected source bytes retain existing handling; no replacement of invalid scientific points or new CRC generation.

Actual extracted NetFramePublish -> typed API -> pool/queue path counted 0 parser and 0 strtoull calls for 96 real encoder cases, compared with 96 parser and 1040 strtoull calls in the old metadata path. This is a reproducible host call count, not ESP32 timing/CPU improvement or a BLE acceptance result.

test_summary.protected_actual_C: PASS: 96 typed real encoder cases, 16 invalid inputs, full metadata/SHORT equality, original byte CRC and immutable queued identity; source/transport ownership, retry/pending TTL and per-sink expiry regressions retained. UBSan enabled.
test_summary.legacy_parser: PASS: 66896 differential cases, 20 original wire fixtures; ASan/UBSan enabled, leak detection intentionally disabled for ptrace environment and therefore NOT_RUN.
test_summary.pipeline: PASS: existing 22 BLE transport pipeline cases.
test_summary.recovery_control: PASS: actual wrapper/internal queue and recovery/lifecycle integration harness.

limits: No target CPU saving assumed from call counts. Parent target build/startup and paired 120s acceptance remain separate gates.
No claim that the metadata POD authenticates arbitrary packets. New callers must retain successful encoder provenance.
No claim that all project P0/P1 are closed: Wi-Fi send/initialization SDK isolation is unimplemented and Wi-Fi HIL is NOT_RUN.
